sections.h2: Harrison County Recorder location and hours
sections.html:
The Harrison County Recorder's Office is at 100 West Market Street, Cadiz, Ohio 43907. The phone is 740-942-8869 and the fax is 740-942-4693. The office is open Monday to Friday, 8:30 a.m. to 4:30 p.m., excluding holidays.

Recording stops at 4:15 p.m. Anything received between 4:15 and 4:30 goes on the next day's business. A recorded document comes back by mail in about two to three working days, and a self-addressed stamped envelope is required for every mailing.

The office does not furnish forms, and only completed documents are recorded. Staff inspect each document and try to have errors corrected before filing.

Harrison County is a rural county in eastern Ohio, with Cadiz as the seat and largest village. It is among the least populous counties in the state: 14,483 people at the 2020 census and an estimated 14,070 in July 2025. Townships and villages all record in Cadiz.

  • Median value of an owner-occupied home: $121,500 (2020 to 2024).
  • Owner-occupied rate: 76.3%, with 7,361 housing units.
  • Median household income: $54,414.
  • Building permits in 2025: 2.

With so little new construction, most sales here are resales of older homes and land, so a clean deed history matters a good deal to the buyer's title agent.

Since October 1, 2022, every transfer is preapproved before recording. The Harrison County Auditor and Engineer adopted minimum requirements for instruments of conveyance so that land is described accurately for tax purposes.

The steps run through three offices, and all three must finish before the deed is recorded:

  1. Submit an unsigned copy of the deed, not the original meant for recording, with a completed Document Conveyance Form. It can go by email to the Map Office, by mail, by delivery or in person.
  2. Wait at least four days while the Map Office, the Auditor and the Recorder review it and return it with any changes explained.
  3. After approval, bring the signed documents in person, by mail, by delivery or to the dropbox. The Map Office forwards them to the Auditor, and the Auditor sends them on to the Recorder.

The Auditor's goal for its own part is 24 hours, though workload can stretch it. If you hand in several documents, say in what order they should be processed.

sections.h2: What the Auditor charges on a transfer
sections.html:
The conveyance fee is $4.00 per thousand of the sale price, with no rounding, and the transfer fee is $0.50 per parcel. Both are due before the transfer is approved. The Auditor accepts check or cash only.

Under ORC 319.202 the grantor pays the conveyance fee and any county transfer tax, while the grantee files the value statement. Every transfer needs a named seller and buyer, an accurate legal description with the full parcel numbers, and a stamp of approval from the Map Office.

  • DTE Form 100 declares value on a taxable transfer.
  • DTE Form 100EX explains the reason on an exempt one.
  • DTE Form 101 is required if the parcel participates in the homestead reduction.
  • DTE Form 102 is required if the parcel participates in the agricultural valuation program.
  • A DTE Attachment Sheet helps when many parcel numbers will not fit on the form.

Splits and combinations of parcels need Auditor preapproval and a minimum of three days. Those requests are made by form and emailed, since they are no longer taken in person.

sections.h2: Recording fees at the Harrison County Recorder
sections.html:
The Recorder charges $34.00 for the first two pages and $8.00 for each page after that, under ORC 317.32. Half of all recording fees go to the state for the Ohio Housing Trust Fund. The statute also permits a document preservation surcharge of up to $5, so call the office for the total before you write a check.

sections.h2: Deed abbreviations in Harrison County records
sections.html:
The Auditor's transfer page lists common deed types with short codes that appear in county records. Knowing them helps you read a chain of title.

  • WD is a General Warranty Deed, and QC is a Quit Claim Deed.
  • ED is an Executor's Deed, AD an Administrator's Deed and FD a Fiduciary Deed.
  • TD is a Trustee's Deed, and SD is a Sheriff's Deed.
  • SV is a Survivorship Deed, and TO is a Transfer on Death Designation Affidavit.
  • CD is a Corrected Deed or re-recording, and MD is a Mineral Deed.
  • AF is an Affidavit, AT an Affidavit Relating to Title, and RW a Right of Way or Easement.

A seller who inherited the house will often hold an ED, AD or TO in the chain. A buyer's title agent will want that document and the preceding ones in order.

sections.h2: Zoning filings and the records commission
sections.html: The Recorder serves on the county records commission, which decides how long county records are kept and when they may be disposed of. Each year the office notifies the county commissioners and township trustees of their duty to file zoning resolutions, maps and amendments. Those zoning filings can matter to a seller with land in one of the 15 townships.

sections.h2: Mineral rights on Harrison County deeds
sections.html:
They can show up. Harrison County sits over the Utica shale, and its history includes oil finds near Jewett in 1895 and the Scio area in 1898. Because of that, a deed may reserve or convey minerals separately from the surface.

The Auditor's list of common deed types includes a Mineral Deed, along with the General Warranty Deed, Quit Claim Deed, Survivorship Deed, Transfer on Death Designation Affidavit and others. The state recorders' fee table also lists a claim to preserve mineral interests as a recordable item.

  • Ask the title company whether minerals were reserved in an earlier deed.
  • Ask whether any oil and gas lease is of record on the parcel.
  • Make sure the new deed states exactly what is conveyed.

The Recorder offers an online records search through Kofile's CountyFusion and a newer cloud search at harrison.oh.publicsearch.us. A Property Alert service is also listed on the Recorder's page.

If you ask for copies by mail, the Recorder charges $2.00 per page, and payment is due before the copies are sent. To find a record, give the owner's name, the volume and page, or the subdivision, lot, township, range and section.

sections.h2: Putting it together for a Harrison County seller
sections.html: Start with the Map Office, because nothing moves until the unsigned deed is approved. Plan on at least four days for that review. Once approved, sign before a notary, pay the Auditor's fees by check or cash, and let the Map Office pass the documents along. The Recorder then files the deed and mails it back within about two to three working days. Build that timeline into your closing date.

faqs.q: How long does Harrison County preapproval take?
faqs.a: A minimum of four days. The Map Office, Auditor and Recorder all review the unsigned copy before returning it with any needed changes.

faqs.q: What does Harrison County charge per thousand dollars of price?
faqs.a: The Auditor charges $4.00 per thousand of the sale price, without rounding, plus $0.50 per parcel, payable by check or cash.

faqs.q: What time does the Harrison County Recorder stop recording?
faqs.a: 4:15 p.m. Documents received after that until 4:30 p.m. are recorded the next business day.

faqs.q: Does the Harrison County Recorder supply deed forms?
faqs.a: No. The Recorder's office does not furnish forms. The Auditor does not prepare deeds either and recommends a legal representative for a transfer.

faqs.q: Can I get a copy of discharge papers in Harrison County?
faqs.a: Yes. Certified copies of military discharge papers are free to the person discharged, and certified copies of DD214s go to funeral homes.
